observation.description: A2-08 (previously loaded history readable offline) is an explicit GAP on this arm: in sessions mode every channel query is authority-scoped, and the JS/React arm's default durable store refuses protected retention with the exact fact on the handle — retention {retainable:false, code:'SNAPBACK_RETENTION_NOT_RETAINABLE', reason:'authority-scoped query: retained display requires the LLP 0043/0053 lease machinery (Contract arm); protected queries are never cold-retained on this arm'} while rqsStoreInfo shows a durable file store present. The refusal is honest, coded, and carried on the handle rather than silently acting local-first — but the product outcome is that a sessions-mode chat has no offline history on the JS/React arm.

competitorOutcome.description: The frozen Convex chat arm also recorded cold offline history as a GAP (reactive cache did not survive a cold offline boot), so no frozen competitor wins this fact today; Firebase's offline persistence is the strongest reference on the adjacent A1 contract.

mustNotRegress: The retainability boundary itself: protected rows must never be cold-retained without the lease machinery, and the handle must keep naming the refusal instead of silently degrading.
smallestCoherentFix: The already-owned lease-custody lane for the JS arm (capability index GAP row sync.offline-js-arm-protected): authorized-lease-bounded retention for sessions-scoped live queries, per LLP 0043/0053.
acceptanceWitness: A sessions-mode client cold-boots with the backend unreachable and renders previously loaded channel history marked retained, then deletes it exactly at the lease deadline; Mallory's store never retains the private channel.
